decision: Use address-only chip selects from latched A0-A7 and A8-A12
options: Rejected AS-qualified final selects; rejected latching selects through DS except special adapters
notes: Figure 4 shows AS only marks the low-address latch window and DS marks the data-transfer window; final chip selects are combinational decode and DS qualifies enables

decision: Confirm physical gate packing for generic gates in New_Address_Decode.dig
options: Current staged 7408 7411 7432 7404 mapping; alternate NAND NOR packing; PAL implementation
notes: The design file names logical gates while the CSV now stages one conservative TTL implementation

decision: Use increasing select codes for increasing baud rates
notes: With MC6850 divide-by-64 this gives 300 600 4800 9600 baud and with divide-by-16 this gives 1200 2400 19200 38400 baud

decision: Use inventory Hitachi HD74LS153P for the baud mux
options: LS TTL 74153-compatible DIP-16 selected; Fairchild 74F153PC parts remain inventory alternates
notes: The LS TTL selection drives the BAUD_SEL_A and BAUD_SEL_B pull-down value choice

decision: Use a two-position DIP switch for 74153 select inputs
options: DIP switch selected; rejected 7474 register I2C GPIO expander and CPU port options
notes: SW2 drives BAUD_SEL_A as the low bit and BAUD_SEL_B as the high bit; open switch is logic 0 through pulldown and closed switch is logic 1

decision: Use 1k0 pull-downs for BAUD_SEL_A and BAUD_SEL_B
options: 1k0 selected for LS TTL HD74LS153P select inputs
notes: R9 and R10 pull open DIP-switch positions low while closed switch positions drive the selected bit high

decision: Keep the 5 MHz crystal loop local to the CPU
options: Place Y1 C5 C6 and R5 close to U1 pins 39 and 38; do not hang other loads on OSC2; omit first-revision SYSCLK observation
notes: Raw oscillator nodes should not be used as general board clocks and no board subsystem needs CPU clock distribution

decision: Confirm CPU crystal load capacitor values
options: 18 pF NP0/C0G initial build value; adjust within COSC1 15-30 pF and COSC2 15-25 pF datasheet ranges; tune for selected crystal load capacitance
notes: C5 and C6 stage the shared-chat 18 pF start value

decision: Omit LI debug test pad
options: Leave LI unconnected; add no test pad or debug header pin
notes: LI only indicates instruction fetch versus data access and is not useful enough for first-revision debug visibility

decision: Omit SYSCLK test point in the first revision
options: Use AS DS R/~W and chip-select test pads for board-level debug; do not expose raw oscillator nodes
notes: No board subsystem needs CPU clock distribution and the staged debug points are sufficient for first-revision bring-up

decision: Stage first-revision bring-up test pads
options: Power rails; reset; shared IRQ; AS DS R/~W; ROM RAM ACIA RTC selects; ACIA TTL serial; RTC timing strobes and BUSY
notes: Test pads are represented as explicit components so the KiCad import can place them

decision: Use J3 as the Port A and Port B GPIO breakout
notes: Port B labels appear on the header while the canonical staged nets remain D0-D7 because PB is multiplexed with the external bus

decision: Choose the exact J3 mechanical footprint
options: Right-angle 2x10 0.1 inch header; boxed or shrouded IDC if board space allows; unshrouded right-angle header
notes: J3 is staged with an IDC-style horizontal footprint as a starting point but the exact connector remains a layout decision

decision: Omit the PA0 activity LED network
options: No PA0 jumper LED or 1 kohm resistor staged in this slice
notes: Current user direction supersedes the shared-chat optional PA0 activity LED proposal

decision: Omit priority encoder hardware in the first revision
options: Firmware polls device status; add hardware prioritization later only if needed
notes: Shared line source identification is handled in firmware

decision: Use 4.7 kohm for the shared IRQ pull-up
options: 4.7 kohm selected; 10 kohm rejected
notes: R8 uses the stronger pull-up because IRQ is exposed on J4 while the low-state current remains about 1 mA

decision: Require conversion before push-pull interrupt sources join IRQ
options: Open-collector transistor; open-drain gate; diode/transistor isolation
notes: Only open-drain/open-collector outputs can directly wire-OR onto IRQ

decision: Decide whether MSM58321 BUSY should join IRQ
options: Leave RTC_BUSY separate; tie RTC_BUSY into IRQ; expose RTC_BUSY only on a test pad
notes: MSM58321 has no normal interrupt output; BUSY is open-drain but should join IRQ only by deliberate design choice

decision: Use one shared active-low IRQ line with open-drain sources
options: MC6850 direct; MSM58321 BUSY only if explicitly selected; future push-pull sources need local open-drain conversion
notes: R8 pulls IRQ to 5V0 and firmware polls status to identify the source

decision: Use JLCPCB fabrication with JLCPCB assembly preferred for surface-mount parts
options: Prefer JLCPCB assembly for all surface-mount parts; prefer Basic parts for ordinary passives; use Extended parts when suitable; hand assemble through-hole ICs sockets headers and other mechanical parts
notes: The board is still designed for bench-friendly hand completion after JLCPCB places the SMD population

decision: Use spare gates for DS-qualified memory read and RAM write enables
options: ~MEMRD = ~(DS & R/~W); ~RAMWE = ~(DS & CPU_WRITE)
notes: U13 gate 4 forms MEMRD_ACTIVE; U14 gate 2 forms RAMWE_ACTIVE with its third input tied high; U32 gates 4 and 6 invert the active-high terms; no new package required

decision: Omit brownout supervision
options: Simple RC power-up/manual reset only; no voltage supervisor; no 7414-buffered cleanup
notes: Hobbyist SBC use does not require long-running embedded-control brownout recovery; the user manual warns power-on reset is for power-up rather than supply-dip detection

decision: Use a 10 ms class RC reset hold time
options: 10 kohm pull-up with 1.0 uF reset capacitor; MC146805E2 tRL minimum is 1.5 us at 5 MHz
notes: R4 and C4 give about one 10 ms time constant which is comfortably above the CPU reset pulse-width minimum

decision: Use simple RC reset with a manual pushbutton
options: External 10 kohm pull-up to 5V0; 1.0 uF capacitor to GND; normally-open reset pushbutton to GND
notes: The manual sample provides the RC reset concept and 1.0 uF typical capacitor; external pull-up avoids relying on HMOS-only internal pull-up behavior for the E2

decision: Use a trigger and read-back adapter instead of transparent RTC bus cycles
options: Latch-and-sequence adapter selected; direct CPU D0-D3 to MSM58321 bus rejected for 5 MHz operation
notes: The CPU writes adapter address data and command registers then polls status and reads the captured RTC nibble

decision: Use A1-A0 subregisters inside the RTC address range
options: 00 address write latch; 01 data write latch or readback latch; 10 command write or status read
notes: Command D1 selects write when high and read when low; any command-register write starts the sequenced RTC transaction

decision: Generate RTC ADDRESS_WRITE READ WRITE and SELECT with an MC14411-clocked one-hot sequencer
options: Direct AS/DS control and 74123 R/C stretching rejected; inventory 74174 7474 7432 7408 and 7404 logic selected
notes: CPU command writes latch a start request; MC14411 F1 clocks U28 through address gap and data phases

decision: Use Abracon AB38T-32.768KHZ-B7 for the RTC crystal
options: DigiKey 535-AB38T-32.768KHZ-B7-ND selected; 32.768 kHz; 12.5 pF load; 30 kohm ESR; through-hole cylindrical can
notes: Matches the MSM58321 requirement for a 32.768 kHz crystal with impedance no more than 30 kohm

decision: Use MC14411 F1 sequencer ticks for RTC timing
options: One F1 tick for ADDRESS_WRITE; one gap tick; two F1 ticks for READ or WRITE; RTC_SELECT is high across active sequencer phases
notes: With X64 baud mode BAUD_F1 is 614.4 kHz so one tick is about 1.63 us and two data ticks are about 3.25 us

decision: Use fixed RTC crystal passives and omit the trimmer
options: C7=18 pF; C8=18 pF; R6=10 Mohm RFB; R12=200 kohm RS; C9 trimmer omitted
notes: MSM58321 Figure 8 gives RFB 10 Mohm typ and RS 200 kohm typ but does not specify C1/C2 values; fixed NP0/C0G capacitors are selected for the 12.5 pF crystal and hobby SBC accuracy needs

decision: Define RTC interface behavior while main logic power is absent
options: Hold RTC chip selects inactive; isolate data and control bus with glue; rely on main-rail pull-ups and inactive CPU
notes: The backed-up RTC supply must not let an unpowered logic bus drive or corrupt the RTC interface

decision: Use battery-backed RTC supply
options: Direct 5V0 rejected; CR2032 plus 5V0 diode-OR into RTC_VDD
notes: RTC_VDD is now staged from Schottky-isolated 5V0 and CR2032 feeds

decision: Keep RTC interface pull-ups on the main logic rail
options: Use 5V0 for RTC data/control pull-ups; do not pull interface lines to RTC_VDD
notes: The battery-backed rail should preserve timekeeping only and not back-power logic interfaces

decision: Hold MSM58321 CS1 and CS2 with sequencer-derived RTC_SELECT
options: Use U33 to OR active U28 sequencer phases; do not drive MSM58321 selects directly from address-only RTCCS
notes: U29 holds CPU-side RTC_CYCLE for adapter register access while U28 and U33 drive the slow RTC transaction select

decision: Tie MSM58321 STOP low and keep RTC_BUSY separate from IRQ
options: STOP low keeps normal timekeeping active; RTC_BUSY is pulled up and exposed through adapter status and test pad
notes: User selected the simplest RTC STOP policy after reviewing the datasheet behavior

decision: Use the MC14411 X64 output range for the baseline serial baud path
options: Selected: X64 with F1 at 614.4 kHz and MC6850 divide-by-64 for 9600 baud; rejected: X16 with F1 at 153.6 kHz and MC6850 divide-by-16
notes: Later discussion resolved the conflict in favor of the existing X64 staging; U3 RSA and RSB remain tied high and F1/F3/F8/F9 remain the mux candidates

decision: Use DIP switch baud mux control
options: DIP switch controls BAUD_SEL_A and BAUD_SEL_B
notes: Increasing switch bit pattern selects increasing baud rates through the F9 F8 F3 F1 mux order

decision: Stage baseline console settings for X64 baud path
options: 9600 baud 8N1 from MC14411 F1 at 614.4 kHz with MC6850 divide-by-64
notes: Later discussion selects the X64 choice already staged in design/baud-rate.md and the netlist connections

decision: Use a DCE-style female DE-9 connector for the serial console
options: Female board-edge DE-9; SBC TX on pin 2; SBC RX on pin 3; GND on pin 5; exact footprint and orientation TBD; handshake pins NC
notes: This favors straight-through cables to modern PC or USB-RS232 DTE adapters; a dumb terminal would need a null-modem or gender adapter

decision: Use inventory Maxim MAX232CPE with 1.0 uF external capacitors
options: MAX232CPE DIP-16; C12-C16 are 1.0 uF per datasheet C1-C5 recommendation
notes: Inventory photo identifies a Maxim MAX232CPE; the local MAX232CPE datasheet recommends 1.0 uF for C1 C2 C3 C4 and C5 on classic MAX232

decision: Use no hardware flow control for baseline console
options: Tie CTS low; tie DCD low; leave RTS NC or test pad
notes: U2 CTS and DCD are tied low while RTS is staged NC

decision: Keep SYSCLK off the TIMER header and debug pads
options: No SYSCLK on TIMER header; no separate SYSCLK test pad in the first revision
notes: AS DS R/~W and chip-select pads cover board-level debug while raw oscillator nodes remain unexposed

decision: Use TIMER header for external slow timer injection
options: External slow source into TIMER; no off-board bus assumptions
notes: J4 exposes TIMER GND and optional IRQ only

decision: Use a small three-pin TIMER IRQ GND service header
options: TIMER on pin 1; IRQ on pin 2; GND on pin 3
notes: J4 stages optional IRQ access beyond the shared test pad while keeping off-board assumptions minimal

decision: Terminate USB-C configuration pins for a non-PD sink
options: CC1 has independent 5.1 kohm Rd to GND; CC2 or VCONN has independent 5.1 kohm Rd to GND; do not tie CC pins together; do not source VCONN
notes: R1 and R2 stage separate Rd pull-downs for orientation detection without USB-PD

decision: Choose exact edge-mounted USB-C receptacle footprint
options: Board-edge connector selected; JLCPCB Extended C2765186 candidate; hand-soldered connector fallback
notes: J1 remains footprint-TBD because the KiCad symbol pin map must match the selected connector footprint before import

decision: Use 10 uF protected-rail input bulk capacitance
options: JLCPCB Basic C15850 selected; 10 uF 25 V X5R 0805
notes: C1 is a component-side SMD part for JLCPCB assembly

decision: Decide whether to add an input power switch
options: No switch; switch after PPTC on protected 5V0; switch before PPTC on USB_VBUS
notes: The shared chat listed a power switch as optional; no switch component is staged yet

decision: Use Littelfuse MINISMDC125F/16-2 for USB input protection
options: JLCPCB Extended C15156 selected; 1.25 A hold; 2.5 A trip; 16 V max; 1812
notes: No suitable Basic 1 A class PPTC was found in the current JLCPCB catalog snapshot; Extended assembly is acceptable for protection parts

decision: Tie USB shield to GND through 1 nF parallel 1 Mohm
options: C3 JLCPCB Basic C1523; R3 JLCPCB Basic C17514
notes: Provides RF coupling and DC bleed without hard-shorting the connector shell to logic ground

decision: Specify expected external USB-C supply rating
options: Dedicated 5 V supply rated at least 1.5 A; preferably 3 A; lower-current supplies not recommended
notes: Power-only non-PD USB-C uses advertised default current without negotiation

decision: Use RealChip SMBJ5.0A for VBUS surge protection
options: JLCPCB Extended C5457085 selected; 5 V standoff; 600 W; unidirectional; SMB package
notes: No suitable Basic SMBJ5.0A-class TVS was found in the current JLCPCB catalog snapshot; place D1 near the connector before the fuse

decision: Treat unused USB-C pins for power-only operation
options: D+/D- NC; SuperSpeed pairs NC; SBU1/SBU2 NC
notes: J1 stages explicit NC rows for full USB-C footprints; no USB data ESD array is staged because data pins are unused
